question: How did estimates of asteroid 2024 YR4's chance of hitting Earth change during 2025?
text:
The estimated chance that asteroid **2024 YR4 would hit Earth on December 22, 2032** rose from about **1.2% in late January 2025** to a peak of **3.1% on February 18**, then fell to **nearly zero** by the end of February. ([assets.science.nasa.gov](https://assets.science.nasa.gov/content/dam/science/psd/planetary-science-division/2025/2025-05%20Lessons%20Learned%202024%20YR4.pdf?utm_source=openai))

| Date in 2025 | Estimated chance of an Earth impact |
|---|---|
| Late January | About **1.2%**, above the 1% threshold for issuing a formal notification. ([assets.science.nasa.gov](https://assets.science.nasa.gov/content/dam/science/psd/planetary-science-division/2025/2025-05%20Lessons%20Learned%202024%20YR4.pdf?utm_source=openai)) |
| February 7 | NASA reported **2.3%**. ([science.nasa.gov](https://science.nasa.gov/blogs/planetary-defense/2025/02/07/nasa-continues-to-monitor-orbit-of-near-earth-asteroid-2024-yr4/?utm_source=openai)) |
| February 18 | The estimate peaked at **3.1%** for NASA and **2.8%** for the European Space Agency (ESA). ([science.nasa.gov](https://science.nasa.gov/blogs/planetary-defense/2025/02/19/dark-skies-bring-new-observations-of-asteroid-2024-yr4-lower-impact-probability/?utm_source=openai)) |
| February 24–25 | NASA reported **0.004%** and ESA reported **0.001%**. Both concluded the asteroid posed no significant threat to Earth. ([science.nasa.gov](https://science.nasa.gov/blogs/planetary-defense/2025/02/24/latest-calculations-conclude-asteroid-2024-yr4-now-poses-no-significant-threat-to-earth-in-2032-and-beyond/?utm_source=openai)) |

The asteroid’s path didn’t change; astronomers’ estimates of it did. Early observations narrowed the range of possible paths while Earth was still in that range, so a larger share of the remaining paths led to an impact. Further observations ruled out almost all of those paths. NASA’s later 2025 updates about a possible **Moon** impact did not raise the risk to Earth. ([blogs.esa.int](https://blogs.esa.int/rocketscience/2025/02/19/2024-yr4-surpasses-apophis-as-riskiest-asteroid-ever-detected/?utm_source=openai))
